strings.d1.s0.name: Koutoubia Mosque
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 77 m minaret, twin of Seville's Giralda. See it from outside, stroll the gardens and use it as your compass in the medina.
strings.d1.s1.name: Bahia Palace
strings.d1.s1.tips: A 19th-century vizier's palace with cedar ceilings and courtyards. It is quiet in the first hour.
strings.d1.s2.name: Saadian Tombs
strings.d1.s2.tips: 16th-century mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, with Carrara marble.
strings.d1.s3.name: Souks Marrakech
strings.d1.s3.tips: Labyrinthine markets selling leather (the Bab Debbagh tanneries), lamps and carpets. Offer a third of the first price and decline offers of a guide.
strings.d1.s4.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa Gece
strings.d1.s4.tips: A UNESCO-listed square with 100+ food stalls (harira soup, merguez, snails), storytellers and the Café de France terrace. Snake charmers will ask for money.
strings.d1.b0.name: Le Jardin Secret
strings.d1.b0.tips: A restored riad garden and tower: shade instead of the souks.
strings.d1.b1.name: Nomad Marrakech
strings.d1.b1.tips: Modern Moroccan food on a rooftop at Rahba Kedima. Book ahead.
strings.d2.s0.name: Jardin Majorelle
strings.d2.s0.tips: A cobalt-blue villa and cactus garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Buy tickets online for the 08:00 opening (they sell out). The Berber museum is included.
strings.d2.s1.name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent
strings.d2.s1.tips: The museum next door. Combined tickets are available, and there is a cafeteria.
strings.d2.s2.name: Gueliz Avenue Mohammed V
strings.d2.s2.tips: The French-built new town, with galleries and the 33 Rue Majorelle concept store.
strings.d2.s3.name: Grand Café de la Poste
strings.d2.s4.name: Menara Gardens
strings.d2.s4.tips: A 12th-century pool and pavilion. In winter you get views of the snowy Atlas peaks, and it is lovely at sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Amal Women's Training Center
strings.d2.b0.tips: A restaurant run by a women's cooperative. Couscous on Fridays.
strings.d2.b1.name: Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam
strings.d2.b1.tips: A shady park beside the medina, close by if you skip Menara.
strings.d3.s0.name: Imlil
strings.d3.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by taxi or tour (1,740 m). A Berber village at the foot of Toubkal, with mules and walnut trees.
strings.d3.s1.name: Aroumd Village Walk
strings.d3.s1.tips: A 1-hour climb from Imlil (guide 200 MAD). Terraced gardens and views of Toubkal, with snow in winter.
strings.d3.s2.name: Berber Home Lunch
strings.d3.s2.tips: Tagine and mint tea in a family home, with a terrace.
strings.d3.s3.name: Kasbah du Toubkal
strings.d3.s3.tips: Tea on the terrace of a mountain kasbah, with valley views. Proceeds support charity.
strings.d3.s4.name: Imlil Waterfall
strings.d3.s4.tips: A short walk above the village. Head back at 17:00.
strings.d3.b0.name: Ourika Valley Setti Fatma
strings.d3.b0.tips: An alternative valley: a 7-waterfall hike and riverside tagine. More touristy.
strings.d3.b1.name: Café Aksaoual Imlil
strings.d3.b1.tips: A café on the village square.
strings.d4.s0.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 14th-century madrasa with zellij tilework, a cedar courtyard and 130 student cells. Restored.
strings.d4.s1.name: Maison de la Photographie
strings.d4.s1.tips: Moroccan photographs from 1870 to 1950. Have coffee on the rooftop terrace, with medina views.
strings.d4.s2.name: Le Jardin Marrakech
strings.d4.s2.tips: A restaurant in a green courtyard with tortoises, in Sidi Abdelaziz.
strings.d4.s3.name: Hammam de la Rose
strings.d4.s3.tips: A traditional hammam with black soap, a scrub mitt and an argan massage. Men and women have separate hours.
strings.d4.s4.name: Terrasse des Épices
strings.d4.s4.tips: A rooftop restaurant with sunset views over the medina and tagine.
strings.d4.b0.name: Hammam Mouassine
strings.d4.b0.tips: A local public hammam. It is cheap, so bring your own scrub mitt.
strings.d4.b1.name: Dar Cherifa
strings.d4.b1.tips: A 16th-century riad café and gallery with a literary bent.
strings.d5.s0.name: Skala de la Kasbah
strings.d5.s0.tips: Take the 3-hour Supratours bus (07:00 from Marrakech). Atlantic ramparts and cannons, a Game of Thrones filming location, and seagulls.
strings.d5.s1.name: Essaouira Medina
strings.d5.s1.tips: A white-and-blue UNESCO medina with thuya wood workshops and art galleries.
strings.d5.s2.name: Essaouira Fishing Port
strings.d5.s2.tips: Fresh fish from the blue boats in the port. Haggle by the kilo, and try the sardines.
strings.d5.s3.name: Essaouira Beach
strings.d5.s3.tips: A wide, windy beach with kitesurfing and camel rides. Hendrix legend (Diabat).
strings.d5.s4.name: Taros Café
strings.d5.s4.tips: A rooftop terrace overlooking the port, with gnawa music. Catch the 17:30 bus back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Sidi Kaouki
strings.d5.b0.tips: A surf village beach 25 km away. Go by taxi.
strings.d5.b1.name: La Table by Madada
strings.d6.s0.name: Mellah and Lazama Synagogue
strings.d6.s0.tips: The old Jewish quarter, with a spice market (Mellah), a synagogue and the Miara cemetery.
strings.d6.s1.name: Dar Si Said Museum
strings.d6.s1.tips: A museum of Moroccan carpets and woodwork, with the loveliest courtyard.
strings.d6.s2.name: Marché Central Gueliz
strings.d6.s2.tips: A new-town market for fruit and a quick lunch.
strings.d6.s3.name: Agafay Desert
strings.d6.s3.tips: A stony desert 40 minutes from the city. Camel rides, quad bikes, sunset tea and a camp dinner (tour about 400 MAD).
strings.d6.s4.name: Agafay Desert Camp Dinner
strings.d6.s4.tips: Tagine and Berber music at the camp, included in the tour. Stargazing.
strings.d6.b0.name: Palmeraie
strings.d6.b0.tips: A palm grove on the edge of the city, with camel rides. Close by if you skip Agafay.
strings.d6.b1.name: Al Fassia Gueliz
strings.d6.b1.tips: A women-run Moroccan classic. Try the lamb shank.
strings.d7.s0.name: El Badi Palace
strings.d7.s0.tips: The ruins of a 16th-century 'incomparable' palace, with storks and pools. The Koutoubia minbar is displayed here.
strings.d7.s1.name: Place des Ferblantiers
strings.d7.s1.tips: The tinsmiths' square. Buy a lamp as a souvenir, and have a drink on the Kosybar terrace.
strings.d7.s2.name: Bacha Coffee
strings.d7.s2.tips: A coffee salon in a 1910 pasha's palace with 200 coffees. Expect a queue. A fitting farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Marrakech Menara Airport
strings.d7.b0.name: Dar el Bacha Museum
strings.d7.b0.tips: The Museum of Confluences. Visit it instead of the coffee.
strings.d7.b1.name: Patisserie des Princes
strings.d7.b1.tips: Moroccan sweets (kaab el ghzal), near Bab Agnaou.
strings.note0: Petit taxis have meters (insist on using them; 20-30 MAD). The Careem app also works, and the medina is walkable. The airport taxi is a fixed 150 MAD, and bus 19 costs 30 MAD.
strings.note1: SUMMER 38-42°C: sightsee from 8 to 11 in the morning and after 18:00, and spend midday at the riad pool or in a hammam. The Atlas and Essaouira are cooler escapes. Check the dates of Ramadan.
strings.note2: Stay in a riad (a courtyard house) inside the medina; a porter for your luggage costs 20 MAD. Haggling rule: pay a third of the first price. Offers of a 'guide' and the 'this road is closed' line are scams.
strings.note3: Tagine 60-100 MAD, Jemaa stall meal 50, mint tea 15, Majorelle 170 (online), hammam 100-400. Tip 10 MAD.
strings.note4: Women will be more comfortable covering shoulders and knees. Mosque interiors are closed to non-Muslims (see Koutoubia from outside).
strings.note5: Turkish citizens can stay 90 days without a visa. Carry cash in MAD (from ATMs); cards are accepted at riads and restaurants.
